# Argus patches

Source: crates.io `gpui-pre` 0.3.9, based on Zed revision `93d745668805029476e6d7fbb19652116fed51de`. The upstream Apache-2.0 license and package metadata are retained.

The vendored package omits standalone examples and their media, the package-local lockfile and the unnormalized manifest. The small EXIF fixture referenced by upstream source tests is retained. Source, build resources, license and upstream documentation remain available.

Local changes:

- A position-only notification updates the screen-dependent state and notifies bounds observers without invalidating the entire local scene. Size and scale changes still use `bounds_changed`, including the explicit hidden-start viewport synchronization.
- Native caption hit testing uses the current platform pointer position against the last rendered hitboxes, rather than reusing the preceding mouse event's hit result.
- Paint-cache replay retains native window-control hitboxes along with cursor styles and input handlers. Cached title bars keep their drag, minimize, maximize, and close regions on every frame.
- `paint_image_subpixel` retains fractional device coordinates for continuously translated raster layers and clips through the existing content mask. Regular image controls retain their original pixel snapping. These images carry `PolychromeSprite::AREA_FILTER` in the sprite's former padding field, asking the Windows renderer to sample them by area; renderers that ignore it keep treating the field as padding.
- Decorative images and bars (optionally with rounded corners) can update their bounds in a clean presented scene. Handles expire on full draws, reserve fixed paint layers, and validate window identity, atlas lifetime, clip bounds and primitive type. Cached paint operations are updated with their corresponding scene entries; dirty scenes and interactions use normal drawing. Animated bars snap their sides and baseline to device pixels but keep a fractional top edge, drawn as a one-device-pixel coverage ramp (a vertical gradient), so their height changes smoothly instead of a whole pixel row at a time. The quad starts where the ramp starts, half a pixel above the top edge (but not above the bar's region), so its rounded corners move with the edge; anchored to the pixel row holding the edge, they jumped a whole row each time the edge crossed one.
- Scene revisions and the earliest animated draw order let renderers retain immutable pixels before the animated primitives. A complete paint invalidates the prefix, including when cached views replay into it.
- The runnable counter uses `AtomicUsize::try_update`, the current name of `fetch_update` on the workspace Rust toolchain. Ordering and checked subtraction are unchanged.
- Text measurement reuses matching wrap/truncation constraints and unwrapped text that fits the new width. Truncated or wrapped results cannot answer wider intrinsic probes. Line wrappers are acquired only for actual truncation, and decoration storage follows the number of style runs.
- Inherited text styles cache their resolved prefix, and text without background decorations skips the empty background paint pass.
- A scroll container's range runs from its origin to the far edge of its children plus the end padding and border, as CSS measures scrollable overflow (`content_end` in `src/elements/div.rs`). Upstream measured the children from the nearest one and left the border out, so a child placed before the content origin (an absolutely positioned overlay such as a scrollbar at the padding box) or a bordered container made content that fits scrollable by a few pixels and showed a scrollbar.
- Mouse-wheel notches (line deltas) animate like Chromium wheel scrolling, which the original WebView2 front end used: 100/3 px per line (`kScrollbarPixelsPerLine`), and cc `ScrollOffsetAnimationCurve` with the ease-in-out timing function and the inverse-delta duration (200 ms up to 120 px, 100 ms from 480 px). A notch during a glide moves its target and keeps the current velocity through an ease-in-out curve with an initial slope. The glide advances while the scroll offset is clamped during prepaint and requests animation frames only for the view being scrolled. The innermost scroller that can still move in the wheel direction takes the event; outer scrollers leave it. `ScrollHandle::scroll_by_lines`, `glide_to` and `wheel_target` drive the same animation for elements whose own wheel handling applies deltas directly. Precise (touchpad) deltas and programmatic scrolls apply directly and end a glide. See `smooth_scroll` in `src/elements/div.rs`.
- Taffy 0.14 uses its leaf-layout adapter for measured elements. Opt-in frame diagnostics report layout node counts, measurement time and cleanup separately; normal rendering does not enable the timers.
- A cached view rendering again only because it animates or because a view inside it is dirty replays the cached views nested in it whose cache keys still match; upstream renders all of them again. Only a view that was notified renders its nested cached views again (they may show its state), as does a window refresh. A nested view replays only if it was drawn in the previous frame (its ranges index that frame) and neither it nor a view inside it was notified during the draw in progress. `Window::request_animation_frame` marks its view for redrawing without a notification (`WindowInvalidator::invalidate_view_for_animation`): observers are not called, and the view counts as animating, not notified.
- `Window::with_visual_transform` moves and fades what is painted inside it without changing layout, element bounds or hit testing. The paint operations keep the untransformed primitives and the transforms (`PaintOperation::PushTransform`/`PopTransform`), so a cached view replayed inside a changed transform lands at the new place and opacity without rendering again; the primitive lists get the transformed copies, and draw order is computed from the transformed bounds. Glyphs, images and surfaces move by whole device pixels, where a fresh paint would have snapped them; sprite matrices absorb the move. Under a transform, primitives outside their clip are still recorded, so a later transform can bring them into view. `Window::with_visual_clip` adds a clip of the same kind: it narrows what is drawn without changing content masks, so a cached view inside replays under a new clip, where a changed overflow clip (part of the cache key) would render it again. Clips nest with each other and with transforms; a transform's own offset does not move its clip.
- With `ARGUS_GPUI_FRAME_TRACE`, `frame-phases` also carries the draw's end on the performance counter (`atQpc`, 100 ns, the window probe's clock), the time spent in view `render` calls, the number of replayed cached views, the views rendered and each view's own time per phase; `frame-present` records each present.
- `Window::set_content_zoom` scales a window's content like page zoom in a browser (Argus's interface scale, which the WebView front end applied as WebView zoom): the platform multiplies its scale factor by the zoom and reports the content size and pointer positions in the zoomed coordinates, and the window refreshes its scale factor, viewport and pointer position (`bounds_changed`). Layout, painting, glyph and image rasterization, hit testing and the native caption hit test therefore stay in one coordinate space, at device resolution. The window keeps its size and position on screen. `PlatformWindow::set_content_zoom` defaults to doing nothing and must not call back into the window; only the Windows platform implements it.
- Line wrapping follows the CJK line-breaking rules of the original WebView2 front end. Upstream broke before any character other than letters, digits and a few ASCII marks, so a wrapped line could start with `。`, `，` or `）` and end with `（` or `“`. All three wrappers (`LineLayout::compute_wrap_boundaries`, which text elements use, `LineWrapper::wrap_line` and `truncate_wrapped_line`) now ask `LineWrapper::is_wrap_opportunity` (public, so Argus can test its interface strings against it): never before a space, always after one, upstream's `is_word_char` rule between two ASCII characters, and UAX #14 for a pair with a non-ASCII character (`src/text_system/line_break.rs`, classes from the `unicode-linebreak` crate, which the workspace already builds). The rules are tailored as Chromium 155 applies them to `lang="zh-CN"` text with `line-break: auto` (ICU's normal CJK rules: small kana, `ー`, `〜` and `゠` break like ideographs; `“` and `”` act as opening and closing punctuation; `‘` and `’` keep Unicode 16's East Asian quotation rules), measured in WebView2 for every pair of 110 characters (Chinese and Japanese punctuation, kana, Hangul, Latin, digits, symbols) and 650 strings with context; the unit tests in `line_break.rs` keep a 32-character excerpt of that matrix. Rules that need more than one character of context on either side (long numeric expressions, regional indicator runs) are approximated by pairs. `wrap_line` peeks one candidate ahead for the following character.
- Measured layout nodes can report their first baseline (`Window::request_measured_layout_with_baseline`), and text elements report the baseline of their first line where `paint_line` draws it: half the line height left after the line's ascent and descent, plus the ascent (an empty line takes its font's metrics, as a CSS strut). The leaf layout passes it to taffy as the node's first baseline, rounded to device pixels, below its padding and border. Flex and grid containers aligning items to baselines (`items_baseline`) then line up text baselines, and block containers take their first child's, as CSS does; upstream reported no baseline for measured nodes, so taffy synthesized one at the bottom edge and `items_baseline` aligned the bottoms of the boxes. Rounding keeps the fraction below each aligned baseline the same, so glyphs, whose baseline is rounded to the pixel grid when painted, land on the same row. Measured nodes that report no baseline behave as before.

The owned-window probe exercises normal startup, caption movement, resize, frame timing, and foreground isolation. Remove these patches when an upstream version provides equivalent behavior.
